dataModelNature.statement: Neither DD-02 nor DD-04 describes an RDBMS. DD-02 models Session / Transaction / Buffer as in-memory Rust structures held in DashMap / Arc<RwLock> indexes (DD-02 §6.3.1, §7.3.1, §8.4.1) and defines exactly three durable artefacts: (a) a Write-Ahead Journal / SessionPersistence log appended as JSON Lines (or bincode - both still 【TBD】) with file mode 0600 and fsync on every state transition, (b) periodic Snapshots (threshold 【TBD】, default stated as 64 KiB of WAL accumulation), and (c) pre-commit file snapshots used to restore the Workspace on rollback. Outbox entries are described as an 'Outbox Table' but are explicitly stored in a file on the same filesystem as the Journal tail, not in a database. DD-04 §5.1 states for MOD-API-001: '使用数据 | 内存：无；持久化：无（仅 Session/Txn 间接访问）', and DD-04 §6.2 describes an 'idempotency_store' KV keyed by actor + idempotency_key with an undecided TTL. DD-04 §7.8 mentions Tantivy / redb as candidate index backends. Consequently the atlas must render ER-style diagrams over in-memory structs plus a WAL/Snapshot file, and must NOT invent SQL tables, foreign keys to a relational schema, or SCD policies; there are none.

The documented REST route table (DD-04 §7.11) is: GET /v1/system/health (health check, bypasses IF-AUTH-001); GET /v1/system/info (IF-CMD-001 'system.info'); POST /v1/commands (IF-CMD-001); GET /v1/commands/{id} (IF-CMD-001 'command.get'); GET /v1/capabilities (IF-CAP-001 'capability.list'); POST /v1/capabilities/{id}/invoke (IF-CAP-001); POST/GET/DELETE /v1/sessions (IF-SES-001); POST /v1/transactions (IF-TXN-001); GET /v1/events (IF-EVT-001, upgraded to SSE); POST/GET on /v1/files, /v1/buffers, /v1/symbols, /v1/search, /v1/diagnostics, /v1/context, /v1/tasks, /v1/plugins (corresponding IF). transactionSemantics.isolation: DD-04 §7.5 makes isolation an explicit Begin parameter (TxnIsolation = Snapshot | Serializable) with 'Snapshot (default) / Serializable', delegating the implementation to DD-02 §7. DD-02 §7.6 does NOT define classic isolation levels; it defines optimistic concurrency: BOTH before_hash == buffer.content_hash AND expected_version == buffer.version must match, otherwise the patch is rejected (ERR-TXN-003 / ERR-TXN-002). Conflict detection order is stated in prose as 'Path -> Hash -> Version' (DD-02 §7.6) but the code sketch in the same section checks hash -> version -> path policy, an internal contradiction. Per-Buffer locking is a whole-buffer RwLock (read shared, patch/undo/redo/save exclusive); Range Lock is deferred to P1. Cross-session writes to the same buffer are serialised only by the optimistic version/hash check. DD-02 does not define multi-version or snapshot-read semantics beyond the TxnIsolation enum name.
transactionSemantics.durability: Write-Ahead Log first: every state transition (Begin / PatchApplied / Savepoint / Validating / Committing / Committed / RollingBack / RolledBack / Failed / SnapshotPointer) is appended to the Journal and fsynced before the corresponding effect. Journal file mode is 0600. The WAL record format (JSON Lines vs bincode) is still 【TBD】 in DD-02 §6.8 / §13.6; snapshots are generated asynchronously once the WAL exceeds 64 KiB (threshold 【TBD】). Physical commit writes the workspace via atomic write: write temp file -> fsync -> rename -> fsync(parent_dir); a pre-commit snapshot is kept so a partial commit can be restored. Recovery is deterministic: the Journal is replayed per transaction and a Committing record without a Committed/RolledBack record is resolved by checking whether the workspace files match the patch after-state (all reflected => Committed, partially => RolledBack from the snapshot, IO unavailable => ERR-TXN-101 UnrecoverableOnStartup and manual recovery). NFR-D-002 requires RPO = 0 and NFR-D-001 requires RTO <= 10 s. Outbox delivery is at-least-once with consumer-side idempotency for effectively-once effects.
transactionSemantics.idempotency: Session create is the only idempotent Session operation, keyed by 'actor + workspace_id [+ worktree_id]' via the SessionManager.idempotency_index; a hit returns the existing SessionId, a mismatched key returns ERR-SES-104 IdempotencyKeyConflict. Transaction Begin is explicitly NOT idempotent (the caller manages reuse). Patch idempotency is carried by version/hash: a repeated patch either conflicts (ERR-TXN-002 / ERR-TXN-003, retryable after re-read) or, for an idempotent command, is re-executed through the version check. Buffer Save is idempotent (atomic write, same result when repeated). At the API layer, IF-CMD-001 accepts an idempotency_key for side_effect ∈ {WORKSPACE_MUTATION, PROCESS_EXECUTION, NETWORK, DESTRUCTIVE} and stores it in an idempotency_store (KV indexed by actor + key, TTL 【TBD】, suggested 24h); a hit on a completed request returns the original response with error.code = ERR-BIZ-004 and HTTP 200; a concurrent second request with the same key gets 409 + retry_after.
transactionSemantics.ordering: Physical write order at commit preserves the order of the FileChange list so that dependent patches keep their before/after relation (DD-02 §7.5.3 P-006c). Event ordering: the Event Bus assigns a monotonically increasing sequence per workspace and guarantees at-least-once delivery with ordering within a single subscriber; (workspace_id, sequence) is unique. Durable event persistence writes to the same WAL as transactions (DD-04 §7.2 E-004). Trace correlation: trace_id is seeded from session_id and correlation_id = transaction_id, so all patches inside a transaction form one series.
transactionSemantics.compensation: DD-02 §7.7 defines Saga / Compensation (MOD-TM-006) for cross-Session / cross-Plugin flows. The P0 decision is the Outbox pattern (MOD-TM-007): after commit a Durable Event is written to the Outbox and a separate worker publishes it through the Event Bus, giving at-least-once delivery plus consumer-side idempotency for effectively-once effects. A minimal Saga (Orchestration) inside TransactionManager is implemented, but a single transaction never calls across plugins; plugin-side events trigger plugin-local work instead. Compensation execution itself is the Plugin's responsibility - the Kernel only exposes a compensation command API 'txn.compensate { reason, target_change_id }'. DD-04 adds a per-operation compensating_op: Option<TxnOp> on TxnAddOpRequest and a RollingBack -> Failed 'compensate_fail' transition. DD-02 §7.5.4 P-004 compensates already-written changes by restoring the pre-commit snapshot.

The only Session type in the workspace is ide_kernel::Session - a multi-tab editor session (docs HashMap<u64, Document>, order, active, next_id) with activate/close/next_tab/prev_tab/dirty_tabs. It has no workspace_id, actor, permissions, budgets, active_buffers or active_transaction, and therefore is NOT the DD-02 Session.

ide_kernel::Document - the real single-document buffer: mgr (editcore::DocLineMgr), undo (editcore::OpeBuf), selection, extra_cursors, line_ending, encoding, path, replace_pending. No piece_table, no DocumentVersion, no ContentHash, no BufferState, and undo depth is the constant UNDO_DEPTH = 1000.

editcore::buffer::DocLineMgr - the actual text container: Vec<DocLine> plus next_seq, saved_at_seq, last_modified_seq and caret. There is no PieceTable, no AddBuffer, no LineIndex, so the DD-02 §8.4.3 data structure is not implemented.

editcore::undo::OpeBuf - the real undo/redo stack: blocks Vec<OpeBlk>, cursor, no_modified_index, max_len (oldest entries dropped when over max_len). This is the analogue of the DD-02 UndoStack/RedoStack but stores Ope operations rather than inverse Patches with versions.

ide-shell-protocol: a working JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio transport with Buffer { id, name, path, lines, cursor, mode, dirty, language, undo_stack, redo_stack, cmd_text }, BufferSnapshot, RpcRequest / RpcResponse / RpcError and codes {-32700,-32600,-32601,-32602,-32603,-32001 BUFFER_NOT_FOUND,-32002 READ_ONLY}, and dispatch methods kernel_info / open_buffer / close_buffer / list_buffers / set_active_buffer / active_buffer_id / get_buffer / set_buffer_lines / insert_at_cursor / key_event / set_cursor / execute_command / set_cmd_text / get_cmd_text / complete_at_cursor / edit_via_provider / chat / register_provider / unregister_provider / list_providers - a completely different method set from DD-04 IF-CMD-001.

ide-shell-web implements its own HTTP server on std::net::TcpListener with a hand-written HTTP/1.1 parser ('极简实现: std::net::TcpListener + 手写 HTTP/1.1 解析 (避免拉 axum 等大依赖)') and dispatches ~70 '/api/...' routes (e.g. POST /api/doc/undo, POST /api/doc/insert, GET /api/doc/export, POST /api/read_file, POST /api/write_file). No /v1/... route exists.

ide-shell-web::auth implements a static bearer-token scheme (X-IDE-Token header, 32-byte CSPRNG hex token, constant-time compare, Host + Origin allowlist for DNS-rebinding defence) - a single shared token, not the per-actor credential / RBAC / session-binding model of DD-04 IF-AUTH-001.

INC-07 error mapping table: 25 ERR-* occurrences in DD-02 were rewritten to the ERR-BIZ / ERR-VAL / ERR-AUTHZ / ERR-DB namespaces with 0 residual; the mapping covers only ERR-CB-*, ERR-EB-*, ERR-CR-* and ERR-BE-*, so the ERR-SES-* and ERR-TXN-* namespaces introduced by DD-02 were left outside the unified taxonomy.

DD-04 §4 ID corrections: IF-BUF-001 renamed to IF-INTERNAL-BUFFER-001 and IF-PLG-001 to IF-INTERNAL-PLUGIN-001; IF-FS-001 / IF-IDX-001 / IF-SCH-001 / IF-AUTH-001 are explicitly provisional local IDs with no IFD-001 counterpart; the note also lists IFD-001 interfaces still not covered by this document.

DD-02 §13 traceability matrix - the method-ID mapping in §13.2 and §13.3 contradicts the method definitions in §7.3.1 and §8.4.1 (e.g. §13.2 maps TM-M-003 to commit() and TM-M-005 to savepoint::create(), but §7.3.1 defines TM-M-003 as savepoint, TM-M-004 as rollback_to_savepoint, TM-M-005 as validate, TM-M-006 as commit, TM-M-007 as rollback; §13.3 maps BE-M-003..BE-M-007 to undo/redo/save/savepoint/patch_apply while §8.4.1 defines BE-M-003 as patch and BE-M-007 as reload).

DD-02 §13.6 residual TBD list (UUID v7 generator, WAL format, snapshot threshold, PathPattern algorithm, savepoint auto-marker, active buffer count 64, max_undo_depth 1000, Session TTL default 24h, quarantine queue) and §13.5 cross-review checklist.

gaps.summary: The three crates DD-02 specifies do not exist. DD-02 §5.1 defines crates/kernel-session, crates/kernel-transaction and crates/kernel-buffer; the workspace contains editcore, ide-cli, ide-kernel, ide-kernel-core, ide-shell, ide-shell-desktop, ide-shell-protocol and ide-shell-web. crates/ide-kernel-core/src/lib.rs:3 explicitly marks 'session / transaction buffer engine' as pending work under DD-02. Consequence: every DD-02 table, state machine and method in this file is Designed, never Implemented.

DD-04 §6.2 declares itself the master table of ALL Core error codes, but the ERR-SES-* (17 codes) and ERR-TXN-* (13 codes) namespaces defined in DD-02 are absent from it, and INC-07 lists no mapping for them. The two documents therefore describe two disjoint error taxonomies for the same subsystems.

ERR-VAL-006 has two different meanings and two different HTTP statuses: DD-02 §8.9 uses it for EncodingDetectionFailed (422) and for BinaryFile (422), while DD-04 §6.2 uses it for '编码非法 (UTF-8 / BOM 缺失)' (400). The atlas cannot pick one without a decision.
ERR-BIZ-006 is used for MemoryBudgetExceeded with HTTP 507 in DD-02 §8.9 and for '资源耗尽 (Budget 超限)' with HTTP 429 in DD-04 §6.2 - the same code, different status and different meaning.

The two optimistic-concurrency failures have two code sets. Version conflict: DD-02 uses ERR-TXN-002 (409) and DD-04 uses ERR-BIZ-005 (409). Hash mismatch: DD-02 uses ERR-TXN-003 (409) and DD-04 uses ERR-BIZ-009 (409). Worse, DD-02 §8.6.2 step 4 calls ERR-BIZ-009 'VersionConflict' while §7.6 assigns ERR-TXN-002 to the same condition - the same document contradicts itself.

DD-02 §8.9 reuses ERR-BIZ-001 for six semantically different conditions with three different HTTP statuses: FileNotFound (404), BufferNotOpen (409), UndoStackEmpty (409), RedoStackEmpty (409), SavepointNotFound (404), BufferClosed (410). DD-04 §6.2 defines ERR-BIZ-001 as 404 resource-not-found. A single ER/error diagram cannot represent this.

The Transaction state machine is specified twice with incompatible content. DD-02 §7.4 requires a Committing state (Validating -> Committing -> Committed, with a WAL record per state) and Crash detection keyed on TransactionCommitting. DD-04 §7.5 goes Validating -> Committed directly with no Committing state and no failure transition out of Validating other than validate_fail. DD-04 §7.5 also adds RollingBack -> Failed (compensate_fail), which DD-02 does not have.

DD-02 §7.6 states the conflict check order as 'Path -> Hash -> Version' in prose, but the check_pre_apply sketch in the same section evaluates hash, then version, then path policy. The documented order is therefore ambiguous.

The Session state enum has no cross-document mapping. DD-02 §6.3.2 uses New / Active / Suspended / Terminated / Failed; DD-04 §7.4 SessionInfo.state uses Active | Suspended | Closed. There is no rule for how Terminated or Failed map onto Closed, and DD-02 has no Closed state at all.

Session id format is contradictory: DD-02 §6.4.1 P-006 requires UUID v7 (generator 【TBD】) and DD-02 §13.6 lists the generator selection as an open item, while DD-04 §7.4 S-005 generates a ULID '含时间序'. The atlas must not pick one silently.

Session TTL is stated three different ways: DD-02 §6.7 gives per-actor defaults (Human 8h, Agent/LangGraph 24h, CI 1h), DD-02 §13.6 says '24h 既定' as the resolution, and DD-04 TBD-04-06 defines a 1h forced reclaim on close failure. These are different mechanisms (idle/TTL expiry vs forced reclaim) and the relationship is not stated.

DD-04 §4 note says 'IFD-001 v1.0 が定義しているが本書が実装層へ落としていない IF が 6 件ある' and then lists ten IDs (IF-CMD-002, IF-CMD-003, IF-EVT-002, IF-CAP-002, IF-SES-002, IF-TXN-002, IF-TXN-003, IF-REST-001, IF-PLUGIN-WASM-001, IF-PLUGIN-WORKER-001). The count and the list disagree, so the uncovered surface is not determinable.

The entire documented HTTP surface is absent from the code. DD-04 §7.11 specifies an axum server exposing /v1/system/health, /v1/system/info, /v1/commands, /v1/commands/{id}, /v1/capabilities, /v1/capabilities/{id}/invoke, /v1/sessions, /v1/transactions, /v1/events and eight more paths. The implementation is a hand-written HTTP/1.1 server (explicitly avoiding axum) serving ~70 '/api/...' routes such as /api/doc/undo and /api/write_file. No /v1 route, no IF-CMD-001 dispatch, no SSE upgrade, no MCP endpoint exists.

The durability model is entirely unimplemented. There is no Journal / WAL / LSN / Snapshot / Outbox / Transaction anywhere in the crates (grep for PieceTable, ContentHash, Journal, WAL, TransactionId, SessionState, IdempotencyKey returns nothing), and every file write is a plain std::fs::write with no temp file, no fsync and no rename - e.g. crates/editcore/src/document_io.rs:460 and crates/ide-shell/src/app.rs:198. The documented atomic write (DD-02 §8.5.4) and crash recovery (§7.8) do not exist.

The whole security / audit / observability layer is unimplemented: grep across all crates for audit, trace_id, correlation_id, quota, permission, rbac and allowlist returns no matches. DD-04 IF-AUTH-001 (RBAC, capability policies, session binding, policy store), DD-02 MOD-SM-002/005/007 and the audit record schema therefore have no counterpart. The only implemented authentication is a single shared static token in crates/ide-shell-web/src/auth.rs (X-IDE-Token + Host/Origin allowlist).

The implemented buffer is a different architecture, not an unfinished one. The code stores text as Vec<DocLine> in editcore::DocLineMgr with OpeBuf undo blocks (crates/editcore/src/buffer.rs:115, crates/editcore/src/undo.rs:168), whereas DD-02 mandates a Piece Table with Original + Add piece columns, a LineIndex and ContentHash / DocumentVersion optimistic concurrency (DD-02 §8.2.2, §8.4.3). No content hash or document version exists in the code, so the optimistic-concurrency contract cannot be satisfied without a redesign.

DD-02's own traceability matrix contradicts its own method definitions. §13.2 maps TM-M-003 to commit() and TM-M-005 to savepoint::create(), but §7.3.1 defines TM-M-003 = savepoint, TM-M-004 = rollback_to_savepoint, TM-M-005 = validate, TM-M-006 = commit, TM-M-007 = rollback. §13.3 maps BE-M-003..BE-M-007 to undo/redo/save/savepoint/patch_apply while §8.4.1 defines BE-M-003 = patch, BE-M-004 = undo, BE-M-005 = redo, BE-M-006 = save, BE-M-007 = reload. Any requirement traceability diagram built from §13 would be wrong.

The REST body-size limit is specified as 【TBD: 默认 16 MiB】 (DD-04 §7.11 R-003, TBD-04-08) but the implemented limit is MAX_BODY_BYTES = 8 MiB (crates/ide-shell-web/src/lib.rs:49), with MAX_HEADER_BYTES = 16 KiB. No document records the 8 MiB value.

DD-02 §7.5.5 P-005 requires a 'SavepointRollback' Journal entry but marks it 【TBD：Journal エントリ追加要否】, and the JournalEntry enum in §7.3.4 has no such variant - so rollback-to-savepoint has no defined durable record.

DD-02 §6.7 marks the concurrent active Session cap as 【TBD：環境変数 KERNEL_SESSION_MAX】 and leaves Quarantine queueing as 【TBD：採用するか否か】, while DD-02 §13.6 says v1.0 will implement immediate rejection only. The atlas therefore cannot render a numeric Session capacity limit.

unknowns: SessionId generator is not fixed: DD-02 §6.4.1 P-006 requires UUID v7 (generator 【TBD】, §13.6), DD-04 §7.4 S-005 requires a ULID. No reconciliation exists in either document.

DD-02 §6.8 / §13.6: the WAL record format (JSON Lines vs bincode) and the Snapshot trigger threshold (default stated as 64 KiB of WAL, 【TBD】) are undecided, so the on-disk Journal schema cannot be rendered.
DD-02 §8.2.2 / §13.6: the chunk size (64 KiB vs 256 KiB), the 100 MiB large-file threshold, the LineIndex implementation (fenwick tree vs rope index) and the mmap OS support matrix are all 【TBD】.
DD-02 §13.6: the PathPattern matching algorithm (glob first, then a Trie) is 【TBD】, so PathPolicy semantics cannot be specified precisely.
DD-02 §7.5.5 P-006: whether a savepoint is created automatically on every patch (patch_apply_undo_point) or only explicitly is 【TBD】; §13.6 plans v1.0 = explicit only.
DD-02 §7.3.2 / §8.4.2: the field layouts of SessionMetadata, TransactionMetadata, ResourceBudget, ContextBudget, Savepoint and BufferSavepoint are never enumerated.

DD-04 §7.1: the idempotency_store backend is unselected and its TTL is 【TBD】 (TBD-04-01, suggested 24h); the concurrency rule says a second concurrent request with the same key returns 409 + retry_after, but the wait timeout for the in-flight case is not stated.

DD-04 §7.1 / §7.3 / §7.11: the hard timeout ceilings (command 30s, provider 60s, REST 30s), the publish timeout (100ms), the circuit-breaker threshold (N=3, duration 30s) and the backpressure wait (5s) are all 【TBD】 (TBD-04-02/03/04/09/13/14).

DD-04 §6.2: ERR-BIZ-004 (idempotency hit) is mapped to HTTP 200 with the original result, but the wire representation of an 'error code returned with a success status' is not defined in the §6.4 Wire JSON shape.
No numeric retry count is given anywhere. Every Retry column in DD-02 §6.10 / §7.10 / §8.9 and DD-04 §6.2 is a Yes/No flag; OutboxEntry.attempts has no documented maximum.
DD-04 §7.4: no request DTO is defined for suspend / resume / close (only session_id is implied), and the shape of the GET /v1/sessions list response is not given.

DD-04 §7.11: the route table lists /v1/sessions with POST, GET and DELETE on the same path but does not say how a specific session is addressed for GET or DELETE (no {id} form), and the DELETE semantics (soft close vs hard delete) are undefined.
DD-04 §7.13: the SSE event frame is given as plain text (id / event / data) and not as a typed DTO; the heartbeat interval of 30s is 【TBD】 (TBD-04-11).
DD-04 §7.14: only the file.read MCP tool schema is exemplified; no other tool schemas are derived, and the MCP error response shape is not specified.
DD-04 §7.7 / §7.8 / §7.9: the FsStat response shape, the IndexQueryResponse hit list shape and the PluginInfo field list are referenced in sequence diagrams but never enumerated.
DD-02 §6.7: the maximum concurrent active Session count (KERNEL_SESSION_MAX) and the decision to adopt a Quarantine waiting queue are 【TBD】.
DD-02 §9.1: trace_id is seeded from session_id and correlation_id from transaction_id, but DD-04 §6.4 shows ULID-style trace_id / request_id values; the two id schemes are not reconciled.
The 'Outbox Table' of DD-02 §7.7 is described as a file, not a database table, and its storage format, index and consumer ownership are not specified.
